facts.fact: The Namibian reports in April 2026 that the final draft of the cybercrime bill was circulated ahead of a validation workshop convened by the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology, before it goes to parliament.

NAM.note: Nothing on accessibility for persons with disabilities.

facts.fact: The Namibian published a column by analyst Dianne Hubbard in April 2026 listing flaws in the government's cybercrime bill, and says the Institute for Public Policy Research made a submission to the ministry on its shortcomings.
The Namibian says the Institute for Public Policy Research submitted its analysis of the cybercrime bill's shortcomings to the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology.
facts.system: Institute for Public Policy Research submission

facts.fact: The Namibian says the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology convened a validation workshop on the final draft cybercrime bill in April 2026, and that civil society groups had made written submissions on earlier drafts but many had little or no notice of the workshop.
